What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?

Write your answer to `answer.txt` in the workspace. Provide a concise, factual answer.
I will write the final response to answer.txt in the workspace.

arguments.content:
Looking at the requirements:
- In-place
- Stable
- Comparison-based
- Worst-case: O(n log n)
- Best-case: O(n)

Analyzing common sorting algorithms:
- **Merge Sort**: O(n log n) worst/best, stable, but NOT in-place (requires O(n) auxiliary space)
- **Insertion Sort**: In-place, stable, O(n) best case, but O(n²) worst case
- **Heap Sort**: In-place, O(n log n), but NOT stable
- **Quick Sort**: In-place, but NOT stable and O(n²) worst case
- **Tim Sort**: Stable, O(n log n) worst, O(n) best, but NOT in-place

The algorithm that satisfies ALL criteria is **Block Sort** (also known as Block Merge Sort or WikiSort). It's an in-place, stable, comparison-based sorting algorithm derived from merge sort that achieves O(n log n) worst-case and O(n) best-case time complexity while using only O(1) additional space.

The answer is **Block Sort**.
